tldr: Headlines in all sixteen country buckets uniformly advertise an escalating military war: tit-for-tat oil-tanker and warship strikes dominate every outlet's homepage framing, with 'impasse,' 'confrontation,' and 'biggest wave' language conveying a deepening stalemate. Economic consequences — oil surging past $100/barrel — and any diplomatic dimension are entirely invisible at the headline layer.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to use 'shadow tankers' — a sanctions-evasion label that frames Iranian vessels as criminal actors rather than military assets, importing a legal/punitive register absent from every other headline in the corpus.

Inverts the standard frame: 'IRGC targets US vessels, tankers in Strait of Hormuz' positions Iran as the party enforcing authority over Hormuz rather than retaliating, with no acknowledgment of the prior US tanker strikes that every other outlet uses as causal context.

Alone in foregrounding the geographic escalation of US strikes — 'from Jask to its oil heartland' — framing the story as an expanding threat to Iran's core oil infrastructure rather than a symmetrical exchange of fire.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, all twenty-six articles across sixteen country buckets collapse into a single military-conflict frame — mutual strikes on oil tankers at Hormuz — with no economic, diplomatic, or humanitarian signal surfacing anywhere in the corpus at homepage level.
